newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S ZAMOSC PLANS MUNI ISSUE, TO SEEK AGENT.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S ZAMOSC PLANS MUNI ISSUE, TO SEEK AGENT.

text.p: The south-eastern Polish city of Zamosc plans to issue municipal bonds worth between six and 10 million zlotys in the last quarter of 1997 and will seek an agent for the issue, the city's president said on Tuesday.
Irena Liberacka told Reuters that city officials will likely decide on April 28 the scope of the issue, originally planned for six million zlotys, and begin the process of finding the issue's agent.
"On the April 28 meeting we will propose the larger 10 million zloty municipal bond issue and we plan to start the process to find the agent after the session," Liberacka said.
She said that independent bank evaluations showed that Zamosc could safely issue bonds for more than the six million envisaged in its 1997 budget.
Zamosc wants to use funds from the issue to exchange its fleet of city busses.
